title: What are paraphilias?
summary: Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Lowell) give an overview of paraphilias: what the term means, the difference between a paraphilia and a paraphilic disorder, a catalog of specific paraphilias (voyeurism, exhibitionism, fetishism, partialism, frotteurism, sadism/masochism, pedophilia, somnophilia, necrophilia, scatalogia, coprophilia, urophilia, zoophilia, mechanophilia, klismaphilia), the history of the term from Krafft-Ebing (1904) and John Money to the DSM editions, the Lawrence v. Texas sodomy case, how the DSM is used in custody and sex-offender commitment, possible causes and the limits of research, treatment options, and a listener mail segment.

segments.title: Opening banter and tour plugs
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with tour and live show plugs, then joke about beer bongs and kegstands before introducing the topic of paraphilias.

segments.title: What paraphilia means and paraphilia vs. paraphilic disorder
segments.summary: The hosts define paraphilia etymologically and through two dictionary-style definitions, then distinguish a paraphilia (atypical arousal) from a paraphilic disorder (distress or harm, especially to non-consenting people).

segments.title: Catalog of common paraphilias
segments.summary: The hosts run through a list including voyeurism, cross-dressing, exhibitionism, fetishism versus partialism, frotteurism, sadism and masochism, pedophilia, somnophilia, necrophilia, scatalogia, coprophilia, urophilia and zoophilia, noting the ethical issues with non-consenting partners.

segments.title: Mechanophilia case and the Zoo documentary
segments.summary: The hosts discuss men attracted to cars, including a man arrested for it and a man who claims to have had sex with over a thousand cars, and mention the documentary Zoo about zoophilia.

segments.title: Language, morality, and the history of sodomy laws
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how moral language has shaped the definition of paraphilia, how homosexuality was once classed as a disorder, and the Lawrence v. Texas case that struck down sodomy laws.

segments.title: History of the term and DSM editions
segments.summary: The hosts trace the term paraphilia from Krafft-Ebing in 1904 and John Money's work, its adoption by the DSM in 1980, and how DSM-III, DSM-IV and DSM-5 defined paraphilias, including the six-month persistence criterion.

segments.title: Causes of paraphilias and research limits
segments.summary: The hosts say causes are not well understood, possibly a mix of genetics and environment; they discuss a family study of pedophilia, sampling bias in criminal studies, and the link between childhood sexual abuse and later offending, which is not a guarantee.

segments.title: Legal use of paraphilia diagnoses and treatment
segments.summary: The hosts discuss paraphilia not being a legal defense, sexually violent predator commitments based on DSM criteria, the custody risk of a paraphilia diagnosis, and treatments such as cognitive behavioral therapy, medication and chemical castration.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read a listener email from Maggie to a teacher named Veronica, then sign off with podcast contact info.
